newsitem.title: UK: Freeze supports NWE gas oil, U.S. Gulf arb beckons.
newsitem.headline: Freeze supports NWE gas oil, U.S. Gulf arb beckons.

text.p: Ice on some barge channels and strong heating oil demand gave healthy support to NWE gas oil premiums on Thursday and cargo players studied a heating oil arbitrage from the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
"If you want to skate, it's great. If you want to move gasoline or gas oil, it's terrible," one barge trader said of the frozen condition of some Rhine tributaries.
Freezing weather that has boosted demand for heating oil again kicked the futures market sharply higher, pushing the IPE contract for front month January up $6.75 to $230.50 a tonne.
Prompt refinery grade heating oil for France was well-supported at around Jan +$5/6.50 cif NWE.

Traders said heating oil for German delivery could be $1 higher at around Jan +$7/8 cif NWE due to lack of offers. They noted that while Russians are well supplied, around half the German market is unable to process Russian material economically.
Traders toying with an arb from the U.S. Gulf to Europe were focussing on the U.S. heating oil market opening.
Heating oil barges for first half January delivery remain at around Jan +$1.50/2 fob ARA. Traders said they expected the premium to firm up to around $3 on Friday if the chill perists.
